newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on trade lull.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on trade lull.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower after buyers and sellers showed little interest for trading amid a lack of leads in the market, dealers said.
They said activity was limited to light short-covering by agents who had sold previously to overseas markets.
"As far as Malaysian prices are concerned, overseas buyers are just waiting for price adjustments," said a trader. "They feel the market has gone up too much."
Trading houses were offering the SMR 20 at 308 cents a kg, the SMR CV at 368, SMR L at 348, SMR 5 at 318, SMR 10 at 310 and drum latex FOB at 240.

At the close, the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted February RSS1 buyer at 309.50 cents ($1.25) a kg, down one cent from Wednesday. February SMR20 also ended a cent lower at 305.50 cents a kg.
Traders said sunny skies since the start of January has created an ample supply of latex and other materials, which were pressuring prices downwards.
The INRO five-day average was 240.68 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Jan 8 from 241.32 on Jan 7. The daily indicator was 238.79 against 239.34 previously.
